s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive unsteadiness and recurrent falls with otologic abnormalities
salient_findings: Progressive unsteadiness and recurrent falls over 5 days
Obstructed external ear canals with effusion and cerumen
Bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids and semicircular canals
key_facts: 4-year-old girl of Turkish ancestry
Presented with progressive unsteadiness and recurrent falls
Initial fall resulted in nasal bridge laceration
No prior medical history
Alert and afebrile on examination
External ear canals obstructed by effusion and cerumen
Three-month history of ear problems
Initial diagnosis of otitis media with effusion and tympanic perforation
Partial resolution with antibiotic treatment
Current otoscopic examination showed polypoid tissue and purulent secretion in right external canal
Contrast-enhanced CT showed bilateral osteolysis of mastoids and semicircular canals
Adenoid hypertrophy and mild sinus mucosal thickening
Brainstem evoked response audiometry demonstrated profound right-sided hearing loss

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral osteolysis of mastoids and semicircular canals, and otologic abnormalities

shortlist.label: Mastoiditis
shortlist.why_kept: Polypoid tissue and purulent secretion in right external canal, and history of otitis media

shortlist.label: Chronic otitis media
shortlist.why_kept: History of otitis media with effusion and tympanic perforation, and current otoscopic findings

shortlist.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
shortlist.why_kept: Osteolytic lesions and potential for multisystem involvement

raw.rationale: The presence of bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids, superior and lateral semicircular canals, and the right external auditory canal, along with a separate osteolytic lesion in the dorsal left parietal bone, is highly suggestive of Langerhans cell histiocytosis, which is known to cause lytic bone lesions and can affect the temporal bone and cause hearing loss.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic granuloma
rejected.why: Eosinophilic granuloma is a type of Langerhans cell histiocytosis, but it is less likely to cause the widespread bone lesions seen in this case.

rejected.label: Mastoiditis
rejected.why: Mastoiditis would not explain the separate osteolytic lesion in the dorsal left parietal bone or the profound right-sided hearing loss.

rejected.label: Chronic otitis media
rejected.why: Chronic otitis media would not cause the bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids and semicircular canals or the separate osteolytic lesion in the dorsal left parietal bone.

rejected.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
rejected.why: Erdheim-Chester disease is a rare condition that can cause bone lesions, but it is less likely to cause the specific pattern of lesions seen in this case, and it is not typically associated with otitis media or hearing loss.
